method: The code loads the Spooky Author Identification dataset (train.csv/test.csv) and encodes the target author labels (EAP, HPL, MWS). Training uses AdamW optimizer (lr=2e-5, weight_decay=0.01), CosineAnnealingWarmRestarts scheduler, mixed precision (AMP), gradient accumulation (steps=2), gradient clipping (max_norm=1.0), and weighted CrossEntropyLoss to handle class imbalance. title: draft - 80d95e12
description: After analyzing the four previous failed attempts, I will take a fundamentally different approach by using DeBERTa-v3-large as a frozen feature extractor and feeding the embeddings into an XGBoost classifier, completely avoiding the fine-tuning bugs that plagued the ModernBERT attempts. This extracts rich 1024-dimensional sentence representations capturing authorial style without training instability, and XGBoost robustly learns the non-linear decision boundaries between Poe, Lovecraft, and Shelley. The validation uses stratified 5-fold cross-validation on log-loss, and the final model retrains on all data for submission.
method: The code loads text data and applies a train/validation split (80/20 stratified). Feature engineering includes: (1) stylometric features (punctuation density, capitalization ratio, readability scores, etc.), (2) POS-style linguistic features (pronoun/article/preposition ratios, verb markers), (3) TF-IDF char n-grams (1-3, 2000 features), and (4) word count n-grams (1-4, 1500 features). DeBERTa-v3-large embeddings (1024-dim) are extracted from the penultimate hidden layer using mean pooling. All features are combined (4544 total dimensions), scaled, and fed into an XGBoost classifier with multi:softprob objective. Training uses 5-fold stratified cross-validation on the full combined train+validation set with early stopping (50 rounds). Final model is retrained on all data and test predictions are generated and normalized to produce a submission CSV.
